promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, your biggest bottleneck is time. You are context-switching constantly between product development, marketing, sales, customer support, and admin. 

The ideal PM tool for you must be **low-friction**, **highly automated**, and **adaptable** to multiple use cases so you don't waste time managing the tool itself.

Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by how you work.

---

### 1. The "All-in-One" Workspace (Best for Centralization)
If you want to keep your project management, company wiki, database, and docs in a single browser tab.

*   **Notion**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** You can build a custom operating system. Use it for your product roadmap, content calendar, light CRM (for investor/client management), and meeting notes. 
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want flexibility and hate switching between multiple apps.
    *   **Cons:** Can be a time-sink to set up from scratch (use pre-built templates).
    *   **Pricing:** Free tier is very generous for solo users.

*   **ClickUp**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Extremely feature-rich out of the box. It combines task lists, Gantt charts, docs, whiteboards, and time tracking.
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want standard project management structures (epics, sprints, subtasks) without building them from scratch.
    *   **Pricing:** Free plan available; cheap paid tiers.

---

### 2. The Dev & Product-Centric Tools (Best for Tech Founders)
If you are building software and spend most of your day coding or managing a technical roadmap.

*   **Linear**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Blazingly fast, keyboard-centric, and beautifully designed. It strips away management bloat and focuses purely on issue tracking and product cycles.
    *   **Best for:** Software founders who want to build fast with zero interface lag.
    *   **Pricing:** Free for up to 250 active issues.

*   **GitHub Projects**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** If you are already writing code on GitHub, using GitHub Projects keeps your tasks next to your codebase and pull requests.
    *   **Best for:** Technical founders who want to stay inside their developer workflow.
    *   **Pricing:** Free.

---

### 3. AI-Driven & Time-Blocking Tools (Best for High Focus)
If your main struggle is prioritizing what to do *today* out of a massive list of tasks.

*   **Motion**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Uses AI to automatically schedule your tasks directly into your calendar. If a task slips, it reshuffles your day automatically.
    *   **Best for:** Founders with ADHD, low time-management discipline, or extreme context-switching fatigue.
    *   **Pricing:** Expensive (~$19–$34/mo), but acts like a virtual assistant.

*   **Sunsama**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** Pulls tasks from Trello, Notion, Gmail, and GitHub into a daily time-blocked calendar. Focuses on burnout prevention and realistic daily goals.
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want a slow, intentional approach to planning their day.
    *   **Pricing:** Paid only (~$16–$20/mo).

---

### 4. Simple Visual Kanban (Best for Speed and Low Friction)

*   **Trello**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** The original digital Kanban board. Extremely simple drag-and-drop interface with zero learning curve.
    *   **Best for:** Non-technical founders or those who want to set up a pipeline (e.g., Ideas -> To Do -> In Progress -> Done) in under 5 minutes.
    *   **Pricing:** Free tier is usually all a solo founder needs.

*   **Todoist**
    *   **Why it’s great for solo founders:** The fastest tool for quick-capturing ideas on mobile or desktop using natural language (e.g., "Follow up with Stripe on Friday at 10am").
    *   **Best for:** Getting tasks out of your head instantly so you don't forget them.
    *   **Pricing:** Free version is good; Pro is ~$4/mo.

---

### How to Choose (Decision Matrix)

| If your biggest problem is... | You should pick... |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"I have notes, tasks, and ideas scattered everywhere."** | **Notion** |
| **"I'm building a software product and need fast issue tracking."** | **Linear** |
| **"I don't know what to work on next / I get overwhelmed."** | **Motion** or **Sunsama** |
| **"I want something simple that takes 0 minutes to set up."** | **Trello** |

---

### 3 Golden Rules for Solo Founders Using PM Tools

1. **Don't over-engineer your system:** It is easy to waste a whole weekend configuring Notion databases or ClickUp automations instead of talking to customers. Keep it as simple as possible.
2. **Design for future help:** Pick a tool that allows you to easily invite a contractor, intern, or co-founder later without having to migrate everything.
3. **Use a "Brain Dump" inbox:** Always have one designated place (a widget on your phone or a specific shortcut) to drop random ideas/tasks so they don't distract you from your deep work.
